originalTitle: Rigidity of homogeneous mechanical families with common invariant force means
topic: 数学力学与非线性动力学
abstract: We study deformations of natural Hamiltonians for which all invariant probabilities on a fixed energy shell give the same mean parameter force. In two normal dimensions, a connected jointly C^{2} family of positive homogeneous wells of degree three, four, or six containing one radial member remains radial. No polynomial assumption, central symmetry, or joint convexity is imposed for this classification. A second classification concerns binary quartics near x^{4} + 12x^{2}y^{2} + 16y^{4}: after phase-volume normalization, a connected family entering a suitable coefficient neighborhood consists of rotations of a single well. The radial and nonradial mechanisms are different. The former uses exact periodic actions and, in degree six, a mechanical brake-boundary response that excludes high-frequency escape; the latter uses constrained action curvature through a rank jump. These classifications produce controlled force correctors. Under joint convexity of the original potential and an actual compact selected tail, the correctors imply point selection for damping (1 + 2/p)/t. The selected limit maximizes the frozen phase-volume root, while the physical mechanical energy has a positive t^{−2} leading asymptotic. An explicit radial family supplies a checkable nontrivial set of initial data for the compact-tail hypothesis.

originalTitle: Invariant-average kernels and deformation obstructions for a quartic Hamiltonian
topic: 数学力学与非线性动力学
abstract: For the quartic Hamiltonian with potential Q_{0}(x, y) = x^{4} + 12x^{2}y^{2} + 16y^{4}, we study homogeneous angular forces annihilated by every invariant probability on a positive energy shell. A complete criterion combines ordinary torus means, every rational relative phase, and the physical periodic family crossing the origin at zero separation. Abel inversion removes the doubly even component, while a certified resonant coefficient identifies the binary-quartic polynomial intersection with the rotation line. The unrestricted problem has two distinct conclusions. First, derivatives of actual jointly C^{2} common-mean families must satisfy a common second-force compatibility: pure doubly odd directions are rotational, and a pure even-odd direction with zero vertical value cannot be nonzero. Second, the original C^{1} even-odd complete-null kernel is finite-dimensional. Its dimension and the existence of a nonzero vertical-trace branch remain undetermined. The finite-dimensional conclusion follows from original-regularity entry, compact observations obtained from complete resonant rows, and exact ordinary endpoint gluing. A quartic Peano value trace and a one-way ambient reconstruction refine the result without asserting a full inverse theorem or a nonpolynomial finite-deformation classification.
